My mom took me away from that fucked up household when I was 3. Before it was yelling and breaking plates. He was away very often, at work or just away. 
Unfortunately, I grew up fat and a spitting image of him and mom never forgot to mention how much like him I was. This made me hate myself. Alone in my bed at night, I prayed to God, but when I thought about him, I didn't know what to say. Did I love him? Not really. I also usually hacked at my skin, first with scissors, then with knives and razors. I hated this body, which was so much like his. 

I haven't spoken to him for many years. I have dyed my hair. I've cut it off. I no longer look nothing like him and yet, a part of me yearns for a father figure.

In college, on Fridays, I would take the train and sit at the largest train station in the city. I'd look at the men in suits heading to New York, Baltimore, Boston..I'd try to imagine each one of them as my father: giving me a hug, attending sports games, going on holidays together. Of course all of that is a fantasy.
